{"input": {"clarifying_context": "Customers: Quantum Analytics (large GPU training jobs with variable demand), BioML Corp (batch inference workloads with spiky traffic patterns), CloudScale Inc. (multi-tenant Ray platform needing cost controls), internal platform engineering teams managing shared Ray infrastructure
Business justification: 80% of Ray workloads have variable resource needs and are currently running on static clusters. Expected impact is 60% reduction in infrastructure costs via scale-to-zero, 90% reduction in job queue time during peak loads, and zero manual intervention for cluster sizing. Multiple enterprise prospects have cited lack of autoscaling as a blocker for adoption.
User problem: Users can only configure static cluster sizes in the SDK, requiring manual intervention to resize clusters. This leads to resource waste from over-provisioning during low-demand periods, performance bottlenecks and long job queue times from under-provisioning during peak loads, and no ability to scale to zero when clusters are idle — all driving up costs and operational burden.
Scope: Single focused need — Ray Autoscaler integration into the SDK. Includes adding min/max worker parameters, an AutoscalingConfig model supporting resource-based scaling (CPU/memory/GPU utilization), workload-based scaling (Ray task queue depth), and custom metrics via Prometheus. Also includes a dynamic adjustment API for runtime changes and scale-to-zero capability.
Success criteria: Users can configure min_workers and max_workers parameters (including min_workers=0 for scale-to-zero). An autoscaling_config parameter accepts an AutoscalingConfig model with resource-based, workload-based, and custom metrics policies. Users can call autoscaling_status() to monitor current scaling state and update_autoscaling() to dynamically adjust configuration at runtime. Clusters automatically scale up and down based on configured policies without manual intervention.", "priority": "Undefined", "prompt": "We need to add autoscaling support for our Ray clusters managed through the SDK.
